THESE PETITIONS, COMING ON FOR REPORTING SETTLEMENT, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER

Since the issue involved in these petitions are similar in nature, hence, they are taken up together,
heard and disposed of by the common order.
The petitioner accused No.1 is sought to be prosecuted for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 506 r/w Section 34 of IPC and Section 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.

This petition is filed challenging the proceedings initiated under Section 12 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 by the petitioner, against the husband and mother-in-law of the respondent No.1.

entities.text: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: This petition is filed challenging the proceedings initiated by the respondent No.2-complainant under Section 125 of Cr.P.C. claiming maintenance from the petitioner herein.

5. The parties are present before this Court and they have filed a joint memo, stating that, the parties have amicably settled the dispute among themselves and in terms of the settlement, marriage of the respondent No.2 with the Pavan P. Kulkarni, son of the petitioner in Crl.P.No.1114/2022 has been dissolved mutually and permanent alimony of Rs.11,00,000/- is paid through Demand Draft to the Sri.Pavan P Kulkarni vs Smt.Sarayu H on 11 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63386107/

entities.text: Pavan P Kulkarni vs Smt.Sarayu H
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4 respondent No.2-defecto- complainant.

6. The respondent No.2-defacto complainant has no objection for quashing the impugned proceedings for the offences alleged against the petitioners and also proceedings initiated under Section 125 of Cr.P.C.
7.
The joint memo is placed on record.

8. Though the offences alleged against the petitioners are cognizable and non-compoundable,
however, having regard to the fact that, the defacto-complainant has no objection for quashing the impugned proceedings, it would be a futile exercise, if the accused Nos.1 and 2 are subjected to trial,
since NC: 2023:KHC:28660 the probability of their conviction is remote and bleak in view of the settlement arrived between the parties.
Hence, the continuation of the criminal proceedings will be an abuse of process of law.

9. Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i) The criminal petitions are allowed;
ii) The impugned proceedings in C.C.No.34732/2021, on the file of the XXXVII Additional Chief Magistrate, Bangalore, insofar it relates to petitioner-accused No.2 in Crl.P.No.1114/2022, is hereby quashed.
iii) The impugned proceedings in Crl.Misc.No.283/2022 pending on the file of the I Additional Civil Judge and JMFC, Mysore District, Mysore, in Crl.P No.4464/2022,
is hereby quashed.
